flawed_step: Theorem 3.3 (\label{second}), lines 0285-0291: 'Let C be a code over Z_4. If phi_4(C) is a binary self-dual code then C is a quaternary self-dual code', proved only by 'replace u with 2 and the proof follows exactly' (line 0290). This is load-bearing: line 0314 in the proof of Theorem \ref{big} uses it to force the Z_4 preimage of the putative [72,36,16] code to be self-dual so that Kiermaier's Theorem 1.1 applies.
counterexample: Take n = 2 and the Z_4-linear code C = <(1,1)> = {(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)}. Applying the paper's Gray map componentwise (0->00, 1->01, 2->11, 3->10) gives phi_4(C) = {0000, 0101, 1111, 1010}. This set is closed under addition (0101+1111=1010, 0101+1010=1111, 1111+1010=0101), so it is a binary [4,2] linear code; all its weights are even and all pairwise inner products vanish (0101.1111 = 2 = 0, 0101.1010 = 0, 1111.1010 = 2 = 0), so it is self-orthogonal of dimension 2 = 4/2, i.e. a binary SELF-DUAL [4,2] code. But C is not self-dual over Z_4: [(1,1),(1,1)]_4 = 1 + 1 = 2 != 0 mod 4, so C is not even self-orthogonal; explicitly C^perp = {(a,b) : a+b = 0 mod 4} = <(1,3)> = {(0,0),(1,3),(2,2),(3,1)} != C. C also satisfies the extra hypothesis actually used in Theorem \ref{big}: it is formally self-dual, since L_C = x^4 + 2x^2y^2 + y^4 (Lee weights 0,2,4,2) equals L_{C^perp} = x^4 + 2x^2y^2 + y^4 (Lee weights 0,2,4,2). The precise breakdown of 'replace u by 2': over F_2+uF_2, Eq. (3) reads [c1,c2]_u = [x1,x2]_2 + u(...), whose first coordinate lives in F_2, so proving [x1,x2]_2 = 0 kills it. Over Z_4 the analogous identity is [c1,c2]_4 = sum_i x_{1i}x_{2i} + 2(...) mod 4, where sum_i x_{1i}x_{2i} is an integer mod 4, not mod 2; proving [x1,x2]_2 = 0 only shows this sum is even, leaving [c1,c2]_4 = 2 as a live possibility. In the example with c1 = c2 = (1,1) (so x1 = x2 = (1,1), y1 = y2 = 0) we have [x1,x2]_2 = 0 and the proof's step [phi_4(c1),phi_4(2c1)]_2 = [x1,x1]_2 = 0 holds, yet sum_i x_{1i}x_{2i} = 2 != 0 in Z_4.
reasoning_summary: The F_2+uF_2 arguments (Theorem \ref{first}, lines 0226-0273) check out: eq (1)-(3) are computed correctly, phi_u(u c1) = (x1,x1), and the two inner-product computations correctly force [x1,x1]_2 = 0 and then [x1,x2]_2 = 0, which suffices because the F_2-part of the u-inner-product is genuinely an F_2 quantity. The transfer to Z_4 in Theorem \ref{second} is where the argument fails: nilpotence of u (u^2 = 0) makes the leading term of [c1,c2]_u an F_2 scalar, whereas over Z_4 the leading term sum x_{1i}x_{2i} is only determined mod 4, so vanishing of its mod-2 reduction is strictly weaker than vanishing of the Z_4 inner product. The concrete code C = <(1,1)> over Z_4 of length 2 realizes this gap: its Gray image is a genuine binary self-dual [4,2] code while C itself is formally self-dual but not self-orthogonal. Hence Theorem \ref{second} is false as stated, and the step at line 0314 that upgrades the Z_4 preimage of the putative [72,36,16] code to a self-dual code (the only route by which Kiermaier's self-dual-Z_4 theorem is invoked) is unjustified. The same mod-2-vs-mod-4 gap also affects the converse direction of Theorem 2.3 (line 0198), which only checks products of the form [v+2v', 2w]_4 and never [v+2v', v''+2v''']_4. Stopping here per the counterexample-first method.
counterexample_note: Only the Z_4 branch is refuted; the F_2+uF_2 branch (and hence the fixed-point-free-involution corollary at line 0322) is not affected by this counterexample.
